system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Triphasic interstitium
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: The description of the interstitium as collagen, hyaluronan gel and gel-free aqueous phases: water distribution among the phases, hydraulic radius, gel swelling pressure from glycosaminoglycans and Gibbs-Donnan effects, and changes in oedema. Excludes imaging methods and lymphatic anatomy.

ATOMS:
- MED-PHYS-C05-S1-01.r1a | S1
  ATOM: Around 1% of interstitial water is normally within a gel-free phase.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0089-s17] Around 1% of interstitial water is normally within a gel-free phase through which water can flow alongside collagen fibre bundles with their associated CD34+ interstitial cells.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S1-01.r1b | S1
  ATOM: The interstitial gel-free phase is a phase through which water can flow alongside collagen fibre bundles with their associated CD34+ interstitial cells.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0089-s17] Around 1% of interstitial water is normally within a gel-free phase through which water can flow alongside collagen fibre bundles with their associated CD34+ interstitial cells.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S1-02.r1a | S1
  ATOM: The interstitial gel phase is largely composed of coiled and twisted proteoglycan filaments that are barely visible on electron microscopy.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0089-s03] The interstitial gel phase is largely composed of coiled and twisted proteoglycan filaments, barely visible on electron microscopy but holding 99% of the interstitial water in association with glycosaminoglycans, mostly hyaluronan.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S1-02.r1b | S1
  ATOM: The interstitial gel phase holds 99% of the interstitial water in association with glycosaminoglycans, mostly hyaluronan.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0089-s03] The interstitial gel phase is largely composed of coiled and twisted proteoglycan filaments, barely visible on electron microscopy but holding 99% of the interstitial water in association with glycosaminoglycans, mostly hyaluronan.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: For the purposes of understanding interstitial water disposition, the interstitium has been described as triphasic.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0088-s21] For the purposes of understanding interstitial water disposition, the interstitium has been described as triphasic [19].
- MED-PHYS-C05-S1-04 | S1
  ATOM: Because the collagen triple helix consists of three intertwined polypeptide chains that entangle water molecules (collagen hydration), collagen fibre bundles can be considered one of the interstitial aqueous phases.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0088-s22] The collagen triple helix consists of three intertwined polypeptide chains that entangle water molecules, a property called collagen hydration.
    [MED-PHYS-p0088-s23] Collagen fibre bundles can therefore be considered one of the interstitial aqueous phases.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: The hydraulic radius of a matrix, the effective radius of the spaces within the proteoglycan/hyaluronan matrix that hold interstitial water and solutes of the gel phase, determines the matrix's resistance to the flow of solvent and solutes through that part of the interstitium.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0089-s06] Interstitial water and solutes of the gel phase occupy the spaces within the proteoglycan/ hyaluronan matrix.
    [MED-PHYS-p0089-s07] The effective radius of these spaces, known as their hydraulic radius, is as small as 3 nm in cartilage and up to 300 nm in the vitreous body of the eye.
    [MED-PHYS-p0089-s08] The hydraulic radius of a matrix determines its resistance to the flow of solvent and solutes through that part of the interstitium.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S2-02.r1a | S1
  ATOM: In the triphasic interstitium, the gel swelling pressure is defined as the subatmospheric pressure that precisely balances the suction effect of the interstitial glycosaminoglycans (GAGs).
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0090-s03] The gel swelling pressure is defined as the subatmospheric pressure that precisely balances the suction effect of the interstitial GAGs, and is an osmotic pressure largely due to sodium ions attracted by the fixed negative charges—the Gibbs–Donnan effect.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S2-02.r1b | S2
  ATOM: The gel swelling pressure of the interstitial gel is an osmotic pressure largely due to sodium ions attracted by the fixed negative charges, which is the Gibbs–Donnan effect.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0090-s03] The gel swelling pressure is defined as the subatmospheric pressure that precisely balances the suction effect of the interstitial GAGs, and is an osmotic pressure largely due to sodium ions attracted by the fixed negative charges—the Gibbs–Donnan effect.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: The gel swelling pressure of the interstitial gel phase is an osmotic pressure largely due to sodium ions attracted by the fixed negative charges, which is the Gibbs-Donnan effect.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0090-s03] The gel swelling pressure is defined as the subatmospheric pressure that precisely balances the suction effect of the interstitial GAGs, and is an osmotic pressure largely due to sodium ions attracted by the fixed negative charges—the Gibbs–Donnan effect.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: The proportion of interstitial water in the gel-free aqueous phase is increased in interstitial oedema, and in the most severe cases reaches up to 50%.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0089-s19] The proportion of the gel-free water phase is increased in interstitial oedema, and in the most severe cases up to 50%.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S3-02.r1 | S2
  ATOM: Many tissues maintain a subatmospheric interstitial fluid pressure in health because the glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) of the interstitial gel are normally under-saturated with water.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0090-s04] Many tissues maintain a subatmospheric interstitial fluid pressure in health because the GAGs are normally under-saturated with water.
- MED-PHYS-C05-S3-03.r1 | S1
  ATOM: Albumin is largely excluded from the interstitial gel phase and the collagen phase but is present in the free-flowing interstitial aqueous phase.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-PHYS-p0090-s16] Albumin is largely excluded from the interstitial gel phase and the collagen phase but is present in the free-flowing interstitial aqueous phase and in the lymph within lymphatic vessels.
